Priya S: Quick thread: design decision on quant ABI migration for fp8/int8/4bit profiles. We need a minimal on-disk layout that supports per-layer backouts and fast compatibility checks.

Noah B: Agree. Proposal: immutable profile artifact (v3) with a lightweight manifest that includes per-layer fingerprint + compatibility hints. Keep manifest small so runtime can validate on load.

Yasmine C: How do we handle rounding/table diffs between v2 and v3? Those cause weird tail regressions.

Diego R: We discussed a delta-quant patch format earlier: store base table + sparse corrections. At load, runtime applies corrections in-place. That gives small patches and easy rollback by skipping corrections.

Priya S: I like sparse corrections. Ops concern: atomically swapping tables w/o breaking in-flight KV cache pointers. Need handshake with runtime GC.

Noah B: Implement swap as: 1) allocate new tables in GPU memory 2) quiesce new requests for 5ms (hotpath) 3) flip pointer 4) drain old refs asynchronously. Add metric: table_swap_latency.

Yasmine C: We should also emit a preflight checksum that the migration tool can verify with shadow eval. Example output: {"profile":"v3-smallpatch","model":"rw/13b","fingerprint":"sha256:...","compat":true} (jsonlines). No raw prompts.

Diego R: Validation harness: run 500 sampled prompts through v2 shadow and v3 candidate in parallel, compute token-level BLEU-ish delta and PPL delta. If > threshold, mark incompatible. We can store a short sample diff log (hashes only) for triage.

Priya S: Operational guardrails: canary window = 0.5% traffic, autoswitch to fallback if moving-average degscore > 0.06 over 10k tokens. Also require per-tenant opt-out flag for Dedicated/Private.

Noah B: Question: API surface for profiles. Keep it simple: profile name + `mode` (strict|compat|optimistic). `strict` = reject if any layer diff > eps, `compat` = apply sparse corrections w/ best-effort fallback, `optimistic` = allow large diffs but enable more aggressive quant.

Yasmine C: Add `seed_replay` to profile metadata so QA can replay a failing sample deterministically. That's saved as a short 8-char hex. Documented in ops runbook.

Diego R: Telemetry: emit `profile_id`, `profile_mode`, `swap_outcome`, `degscore_sampled`, `p99_latency_ratio`. Sample by 0.1% for diffs. Do not include user text.

Priya S: Backwards compat: runtime should accept legacy v1/v2 and auto-upgrade to v3 manifest if `--migrate-on-load` is set. Migrations must be reversible.

Noah B: Testing notes: add a fuzz target that mutates quant tables and asserts no segfault + that swap path is atomic under concurrency. Also add perf regression tests for hotpath < 5% overhead.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-quant-abi-migration-1751001234 and scheduled nightly validation job `quant-abi-preflight/1751001234`.

Yasmine C: Docs: include troubleshooting matrix (symptoms -> likely root cause -> quick fixes). Example: tail hallucinations -> check per-layer scale mismatch -> try `--force-sparse-corrections` or run `rwd-quant-replay --sample <hex>`.

Diego R: I'll prototype sparse patch encoding and small loader shim in a sandbox today. Link in thread when ready.

Priya S: Thanks — next steps: Diego prototype, Noah table-swap implementation, Yasmine QA harness + metrics sketch. We'll sync Thursday 10am. :thumbsup:
